- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model often over-optimistic; apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecast if sentiment > 0.4 and price > 80.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4) — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% if sentiment swings > 0.3 in last 3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 80+; if price > 80 for 3+ consecutive days, apply 2–4% downward correction.
- If sentiment is flat or negative (≤0.1) and price is falling, model tends to underestimate — add 1–3% to forecast to avoid under-shock.
- When sentiment is high but price is low (e.g., 70–75), model often overcorrects downward — increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
